content:
Wall Street just reminded investors that stock prices can swing hard, with the S&P 500 sliding into correction territory after several strong years. When markets reset like this, predictable cash payouts start to look a lot more attractive. That is where a group of companies that steadily raise their dividends and earnings, while offering a 2% to 5% yield, can matter. This article highlights three such dividend growers from that universe.

The three examples below are just a sample, and the full screen surfaced 43 more dividend payers with similar payout profiles and business stories that are not covered here. To identify and analyze your own higher conviction ideas among these growing dividend payers, head straight to the Growing Dividend Payers with 2-5% yield screener .

Overview: Copa Holdings runs Copa Airlines, a Panama based carrier providing passenger, cargo, and mail flights across North, Central, and South America and the Caribbean. Its core airline cash flows support a dividend profile that may appeal to investors seeking a 2% to 5% yield.

Copa Holdings fits into this growing dividend payers theme because its hub based airline model generates cash that supports measured, recurring payouts. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St outlines how current expansion plans aim to reinforce that pattern.

"Expansion of Copa Holdings' Hub of the Americas through high teens capacity growth, new destinations and the planned move from 6 to 8 daily connecting banks by March 2027 is set to deepen connectivity across the Americas, which can support higher revenue and load factors as more traffic is funneled through the Panama hub."

The key issue going forward is how one cost pressure interacts with this growth plan and affects the scope for any future dividend increases.

That cost question sits at the center of whether Copa Holdings' dividend story keeps accelerating or stalls, and the full narrative for Copa Holdings explains how capacity plans, capital spending, and competitive pressures all fit together.

Overview: Avery Dennison is a materials science and digital identification company that supplies label materials, graphics, reflective films, and RFID driven information solutions to global consumer, retail, logistics, and industrial customers.

Operations: Avery Dennison generates about US$6.8b from its Materials Group and US$2.8b from its Solutions Group, with additional intersegment adjustments.

Avery Dennison matters for this growing dividend payers theme because its RFID rich Information Solutions business brings recurring, contract based cash flows that can help support a 2% to 5% payout profile. This link is highlighted in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St.

"Expanding Intelligent Labels programs across apparel, general retail and food, including rollouts with the largest U.S. grocer and a ramp expected in the second half of 2026, could lift Avery Dennison's future revenue and support earnings as higher value solutions become a larger share of sales."

What happens to Avery Dennison's dividend path may depend on how one unseen cost and leverage pressure interacts with that higher value mix.

That pressure point is exactly what full narrative for Avery Dennison unpacks, showing where accelerating RFID demand and balance sheet strain could diverge or quietly work in Avery Dennison's favor.

Overview: Brunswick designs and sells marine engines, boats, electronics and subscription services that create recurring aftermarket parts and service income streams.

Operations: Brunswick generates about US$2.3b from Propulsion, US$1.6b from Boat, US$1.3b from Engine Parts & Accessories and US$840 million from Navico Group.

For the Growing Dividend Payers with 2–5% yield theme, Brunswick matters because its Mercury propulsion, Boat brands and memberships turn one time equipment sales into ongoing parts, service and club cash flows. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St argues that this can steadily reshape how dependable those future dividends look.

"Expansion of high margin recurring parts, accessories and services in Brunswick, including a growing contribution from Freedom Boat Club which reached more than US$200 million of revenue in 2025 and over 63,000 members on near 90% retention, points to a larger earnings base that is less tied to new boat cycles and can support future margin resilience."

What happens if a single pressure on Brunswick's balance sheet tightens just as those recurring marine cash flows start to scale up?

If that balance sheet squeeze worries you, the full narrative for Brunswick maps how Brunswick's recurring marine cash flows and leverage could be quietly decoupling in investors' favor.
